name: D. R. Horton
key_signal: DHI trades right at both its 50- and 200-day moving averages with negative momentum (mom_21d -4.4%, mom_126d -5.7%) while fundamentals show shrinking revenue (-2.3%) and earnings (-13.2%), reflecting a housing market stalled by high rates.
thesis: DHI trades at a cheap 14x trailing / 12.4x forward P/E and 1.8x book with a still-healthy 11.3% operating margin and 13% ROE, suggesting the market has already priced in a housing slowdown; if rates ease into year-end, pent-up demand and DHI's low debt/equity (27%) and $2.9B FCF give it flexibility to buy back shares and defend margins better than peers, positioning it for a re-rating once the negative earnings revisions stabilize.
bear_case: The stock is down from a 52-week high of $184.55 to $149.39 (~19% off highs) and sits exactly at both the 50- and 200-day moving average with a bearish MACD histogram (-1.12) and RSI at 44.6, indicating momentum is breaking down, not basing; revenue and earnings are already declining (-2.3%/-13.2%) even before any further affordability shock, and homebuilders are notoriously early-cycle-sensitive — if mortgage rates stay elevated or unemployment ticks up, order cancellations and incentive-driven margin compression could push earnings estimates down further, making the 'cheap' multiple a value trap rather than a floor.
